promptText: What project management tools exist for a startup founder working solo?
rawText:
As a solo startup founder, your project management needs are unique. You don't need complex team permissions or endless status meetings; you need **speed, low administrative overhead, and context-switching management** (since you are simultaneously CEO, developer, marketer, and customer support).

Here is a breakdown of the best project management tools for solo founders, categorized by working style:

---

### 1. The "All-in-One / Second Brain" Tools
*Best if you want your tasks, strategy notes, customer feedback, and documentation in one single place.*

*   **Notion**
    *   **Why it’s great for solos:** It’s an empty canvas. You can build a custom CRM, product roadmap, task board, and pitch deck repository in one app.
    *   **Best feature:** Linked databases (e.g., linking a "Task" to a "Feature Launch" document).
    *   **Downside:** Easy to spend days tweaking your setup instead of actually working.
    *   **Cost:** Free tier is very generous for solo users.
*   **ClickUp**
    *   **Why it’s great for solos:** Extremely feature-rich out of the box. Includes docs, mind maps, time tracking, and task lists without needing to build them from scratch like Notion.
    *   **Best feature:** Ability to switch views instantly (Kanban board, List, Gantt chart, Calendar).
    *   **Downside:** Can feel cluttered or overwhelming ("feature bloat").
    *   **Cost:** Free tier is robust.

---

### 2. The Tech & Product-First Tools
*Best if you are building software/SaaS and spend most of your time writing code.*

*   **Linear**
    *   **Why it’s great for solos:** Built specifically for software development. It is lightning-fast, keyboard-driven, and forces you to work in tight, focused cycles.
    *   **Best feature:** Deep integration with GitHub/GitLab; automations move tasks when you push code.
    *   **Downside:** Strictly tailored for software issue tracking—less useful for high-level marketing or business tasks.
    *   **Cost:** Free tier supports up to 250 active issues (plenty for a solo MVP phase).
*   **GitHub Projects**
    *   **Why it’s great for solos:** If you live in GitHub, it keeps your project management right next to your code base for zero context switching.
    *   **Downside:** Basic interface compared to dedicated tools.
    *   **Cost:** Free.

---

### 3. The AI & Time-Blocking Tools
*Best if your biggest challenge is figuring out **what to do next** and managing your calendar.*

*   **Motion (UseMotion)**
    *   **Why it’s great for solos:** It uses AI to dynamically schedule your tasks directly into your calendar. If a task takes longer than expected, it automatically reschedules the rest of your week.
    *   **Best feature:** Eliminates the mental tax of deciding *when* to work on what.
    *   **Downside:** Expensive; no free plan.
    *   **Cost:** ~$19–$34/month.
*   **Sunsama**
    *   **Why it’s great for solos:** Designed for intentionality and avoiding burnout. It guides you through a 5-minute daily planning ritual every morning, pulling tasks from Slack, Notion, GitHub, or email into a daily schedule.
    *   **Best feature:** Unified view of tasks + calendar with time-boxing.
    *   **Downside:** Premium-only tool.
    *   **Cost:** ~$16–$20/month.

---

### 4. Lightweight & Fast Task Managers
*Best if you just want to capture ideas quickly and get things done without complex setup.*

*   **Todoist**
    *   **Why it’s great for solos:** The fastest task-capture engine on the market. Natural language parsing lets you type *"Draft landing page copy tomorrow at 9am #marketing"* and it sets it up automatically.
    *   **Best feature:** Speed and cross-platform availability.
    *   **Downside:** Lacks deep document storage or rich database views.
    *   **Cost:** Free tier is good; Pro is ~$4/month.
*   **Trello**
    *   **Why it’s great for solos:** The classic, simple Kanban board. Drag cards from *To-Do* to *Doing* to *Done*.
    *   **Best feature:** Very visual, zero learning curve.
    *   **Downside:** Can get messy fast if you have hundreds of micro-tasks.
    *   **Cost:** Free.

---

### How to Choose (Decision Matrix)

| If your primary need is... | Choose this tool: |
| :--- | :--- |
| **"I want my docs, strategy, and tasks in one place."** | **Notion** |
| **"I am building a SaaS product and want to ship fast."** | **Linear** |
| **"I struggle with time management and daily focus."** | **Sunsama** or **Motion** |
| **"I want a simple list with zero setup time."** | **Todoist** |

---

### Golden Rule for Solo Founders

**Avoid the "Productivity Trap."** 
As a solo founder, the best PM tool is the one that takes the *least* amount of time to maintain. If you spend more than 15–20 minutes a day managing your tool, it’s managing you. 

* **Recommended Solo Stack:** **Notion** (for specs, notes, and roadmap) + **Todoist** (for daily execution tasks) OR **Linear** (if pure tech product) + **Google Calendar**.
